blocks.text: **Conditional probability:** P(A | B) means the share of group B that is also in A. Compute overlap / size of B. The group after the bar is the denominator.

blocks.setup: Same 2 x 2 table for both directions. Illustrative count added for teaching: 3 non-commuters cycle.

steps.label: Counts
steps.text: Among 40 students: 25 commute; 10 commuters cycle; 3 non-commuters cycle. Table: commuters—10 cycle, 15 do not; non-commuters—3 cycle, 12 do not.

steps.label: Among commuters
steps.text: 10 / 25 = 40.0% of commuters cycle. Reference group = commuters; denominator = 25.

steps.label: Among cyclists
steps.text: 10 / 13 = 76.9% of cyclists commute. Reference group = cyclists; denominator = 13.

blocks.takeaway: Reversing the condition changes the reference group and usually changes the answer.

blocks.text: Before dividing: underline the words after ‘of’ / ‘among’; those identify the reference group. Assume equally weighted cases and a non-empty group.
Report every proportion as a percentage to 1 decimal place and name the group: ‘40.0% of commuters.’
Row % = cell / its row total. Answers ‘within this row group, what share…?’ Each complete row sums to 100%.
Column % = cell / its column total. Answers ‘within this column group, what share…?’ Each complete column sums to 100%. Percentages across a row of column percentages need not sum to 100%.

blocks.prompt: Need the column percentage for commuters among cyclists.
blocks.fix: Use the cyclist column total: 10 / 13 = 76.9% of cyclists are commuters.
blocks.conditions: Choose the denominator from the requested reference group, not the cell's row/column label alone.

blocks.setup: Illustrative grouped summary of scores by section.

steps.label: Group
steps.text: Compute one mean score for each non-empty section.

steps.label: Output
steps.text: The summary has 4 rows—one per section, not 120 rows.

blocks.takeaway: Compare group means with group means, or counts with counts; do not compare a mean to a total.

blocks.text: A grouped summary splits cases by a categorical variable and reports one chosen summary (for example, mean or count) per non-empty group.
